# Test Set Size in the NMT Search Error and Model Error Study

## Direct Answer

## Source Evidence for the Full Test Set Size

The primary source, document_1.txt, provides the most direct statement. In the section titled “Results without Length Constraints,” it states: “We conduct all our experiments in this section on the entire English-German WMT news-test2015 test set (2,169 sentences) with a Transformer base model...” ([document_1.txt](document_1.txt)). Thus, the full test set size is not an estimate or an approximation; it is a reported count.

The secondary source, document_2.txt, is a third-party research note that summarizes the same paper’s test set details. It states: “The entire English-German WMT news-test2015 test set contains 2,169 sentences. The paper states the test set size as a number of sentences. This full test set size of 2,169 sentences is reported before any subset selection.” ([document_2.txt](document_2.txt)). ## Full Test Set Versus Length-Constrained Subsets

The reported subset percentages are **73.0%** and **48.3%**. ## Methodological and Reporting Considerations

The source material is consistent about the test set size, but it also illustrates a broader methodological issue in machine translation evaluation: reporting subset sizes alongside full test set sizes is essential for transparency. Document_2.txt notes that the paper reports the full test set size of 2,169 sentences before any subset selection and that the length-constrained experiments use only a subset ([document_2.txt](document_2.txt)).
